title: Self-Discipline
tagline: Anushasanam — the gentle art of commitment
description: Master your mind and cultivate unwavering practice through the wisdom of Patanjali's foundational sutras on discipline, concentration, and mental mastery.

sutra.meaning:
Now begins the discipline of Yoga. 
Shasana or discipline is what someone else imposes on you but anushasana or self-discipline is what you impose on yourself. 
One needs discipline to do something which is not enjoyable to start with. You will enjoy yoga only after having practiced it for some time and reaped the benefits thereof.

sections.insight: This is a sacred beginning. When there is readiness the journey unfolds naturally. To ready oneself for yoga mental commitment is necessary. Commitment to bring discipline in your life. Self-discipline is needed in areas which are not so pleasant to start with but give joy in the long term ie. Sattvic matters. In comparison Rajasic activities may give great joy in the begining but bring only misery in the end. Tamasic of course is total lack of discipline. Apply this rule to say, the kind of food you eat or the kind of entertainment you enjoy and you will see why Patanjali called yoga a discipline.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Will I call myself a self-disciplined person or do I need monitoring?
sections.practice:
Find a quiet and comfortable place to sit. Sit quietly and set an intention for daily practice.
Be aware of all you do during the day and see if you will classify it sattvic, rajasic or tamsic.
sections.journalPrompt: Was sitting still in silence difficult?
sections.shlokaFrom:
उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् ।
आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥ ६-५ ॥
sections.wisdomFrom: Elevate yourself through the power of your mind, and not degrade yourself. For the mind can be the friend and also the enemy of the self".
sections.gurudevInsight: Now, we will look into the discipline of Yoga. Now I will enunciate the discipline of Yoga. Shashana mean rules that somebody else puts on you. Anushashana is the rule that you put, impose on yourself.Once it became a habit & when you understood, it is good for you then it is no more mothers’ rule. Like keeping yourself clean, hygiene, exercising, meditating, being kind, considerate, not being rude, all these rules you have imposed on yourself are disciplines, isn’t it? Discipline to unite yourself, Unite all the loose ends of your existence.

sutra.meaning:
Yoga is the stilling of the fluctuations of the Consciousness ie Chitta. The Chitta comprises of the Manas, Buddhi, Ahamkar. The mind, intellect and ego.
Once the chitta is calm then the sadhak abide in their true nature.

sections.insight:
The mind keeps moving. Awareness—not suppression—brings stillness. Yoga shows us how. 
When the mind settles you experience your true self—peaceful and aware.
sections.reflectionPrompt: When is my mind most restless? Am I aware of the constant internal dialogue. Can I differentiate between my mind, intellect and how my identity is intertwined with them?
sections.practice: Bring your awarenes over and over to your thoughts without reacting.
sections.meditation:
10 min breathing. 
Pause and observe moments of stillness
sections.journalPrompt: Did I observe repetitive thoughts? I should watch like I hawk which thoughts are frequent visitors.

sections.gurudevInsight: There are certain vritis of the mind, which are problematic, which cause difficulties & certain others which do not cause any difficulty. Tada drushte swarupe awasthanam - It puts you on to your self, otherwise what has been happening? Vrutti sarupya mitaratra- Your mind is engaged - is caught up in outside world all the time. Eyes open, you are caught up in all that you see.

sutra.meaning:
The chitta is disturbed by five-fold movements of our mind, some of these vrittis or modulations can be painful others not so much however all of them bring disturbance. Yoga is when they are dropped.

They are- 1. It seeks Pramana or validity of knowledge. Is the knowledge experiential, or at least can be guessed at. Perhaps the scriptures say so. 2. However, despite all the proof seeking the mind may still opt for Viparyaya ie. perverse or wrong knowledge, 3. Sometimes there is no truth at all just imagination or delusion ie vikalpa, 4.The 4th vritti is sleep and 5.  the memory of it all. All this keeps our mind busy unless asleep.

sections.insight:
Some thoughts bring a lot of misery some less. Awareness quietens most thoughts.

Pramana is direct knowledge, from the core of ones being. Viparyaya is wrong perceptions gathered by the senses of perception like taking the coat stand for a ghost in the dark. Vikalpa is just being in la-la land without any  basis in facts. Smriti helps one recollect experiences for right understanding and waking from sleep one experiences the quietude ie. the opposite of the disturbed chitta.
sections.reflectionPrompt:
Which thoughts disturb me most?
Which of Patanjali's classifications keeps my mind busy? What happens when observed?
sections.meditation:
10 min meditation.
Observe thoughts as helpful/unhelpful

sections.gurudevInsight:
Pramanaviparyayavikalpanidrasmruti You call it mind or consciousness or chitta – it’s all the same – different modes of consciousness. Five modes of Consciousness arises in your Self. "Pramana - 1st Activity of the mind. Your mind is engaged in wanting a proof. Are you in
Switzerland? Right Now? You say yes, how? You have a proof in the mind?
Three types of pramana –Pratyaksha – anumana, agama. Pratyaksha means obvious – experiencial. Anumana, it’s not so obvious, but you guess, & whatever you guess,
you believe in it.Agama pramana is the scriptures because it is written in black & white, believing in it is easy.
II. Viparyaya :- Patanjali very beautifully described each of these modulations.
“Viparyayo mithyagyanamatadupratistham”. Pramana is the knowledge that the mind is
constantly engaged in arguments, in proofs. This moment there could be arguing, proving there could be some logic in your mind, looking for a proof or it will have a wrong understanding. You will think things the way they are not. Do you see what I am saying? Most of the time you impose your own views & ideas & feelings on others and you think that is how they are. This activity of mind is called viparyaya.
(III) Vikalpa :- It is sort of hallucination. Nothing of that sort exists. Just mere words hover
in the mind. All these fears, all these unfounded baseless mere sounds which do not carry much meaning, such thoughts, such ideas are called Vikalpa – fantasies..Fourth is (IV) Nidra :- When the mind is not in any of the above three, the fourth place,it goes to sleep. (V) Smruti (Memory) 5th activity of the mind. That is remembering the experiences it had had. Remembering the past experiences i.e smruti. Now see, when you are awake, are you in any of these four states of Modulations? "

sutra.meaning: Repeated practice without atachment is the way to still the mind

sections.insight: Consistency and letting go brings mastery. I will not be focused on the end result while I practice regularly.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Can I practice consistently without constantly measuring my progress?

sections.insight: Consistency builds strength naturally. I need to honour the practice.

sections.wisdomFrom: One who restrains their senses and fixes their consciousness upon Me is known as a man of steady intelligence
sections.gurudevInsight: But this effort to be established steadily in the now, becausethe now is not just linear, the now is very deep & vast. Now, it is the present moment. It’snot just a point, just a dot. It’s infinity. It’s all-dimensional, from all sides, directions. Practice is the stability in that moment. That is the purpose of practice & how can thatbe achieved? It takes long time (dirghkaal), without a Gap (nairantarya), with Honour & with Respect (satkarsevito) receiving it & practicing it then it becomes firmly established (drudbhoomi). Anything in life that is of some value takes some time to culture.

sutra.meaning: Practice must be persued with faith,confidence, energy, keenness of memory and the power to absorb to avoid spiritual complacency.

sections.insight: I need to put in my 100% to make progress
sections.reflectionPrompt: Inner growth needs sincerity and effort. Am I willing to make the effort?
sections.practice: Be 100% present in whatever you do today
sections.journalPrompt:
Do I have doubts about the knowledge or my ability to adhere to it?
How present was I while doing my chores today?
sections.gurudevInsight:
Shraddha means faith. Faith creates such a quality in your conociousness. It makes your consciousness stable, steady, solid. Doubt in consciousness makes you very vulnerable, fearful, uncertain, fluid.
Veerya :- it is 100% vigor or force, courage, vitality, total courage, the force with which
an army personal goes, valor, the valor with which army fights ...thrill is a sense of veerya, valor. The entire body, every cell in the body gets united, the whole consciousness becomes one. Defense system gets awakened in you. That is again a strength, defense against fear. That sense of patriotism or valor or vigor, also takes you to a state of Meditation.
 Smruti: means memory of it. Once who have had a very peaceful, beautiful state of mind
experience, the very memory of it again, will again make you re-live that. Memory of Samadhi reproduces, memory of one’s Being, memory of the
Self, memory of freedom, memory of devotion, memory of Surrender, memory of love,
memory of joy, brings back you to your Self.

sections.theme: How much do you want it?

sutra.meaning:
Intense effort brings quick progress
Effort varies in intensity -i) feeble ii) moderate iii)steady

sections.insight:
Depth of desire determines growth. How badly do you want it.

The pace of growth depends on your effort.
sections.reflectionPrompt:
How strong is my intention?
Where am I on this scale?
sections.practice:
Act with intensity
Observe effort level
sections.shlokaFrom:

sections.wisdomFrom: The mind is restless, turbulent, strong, and stubborn; controlling it is as difficult as controlling the wind

sutra.meaning:
There are 9 obstacles on the path.
1.Disease 2. lack of interest. Sluggishness 3.Doubt (in oneself, the process or the teacher) 4.Negligence, knowingly not doing the right thing. 5.Laziness 6. Lack of moderation in sensual gratification 7.Illusion. Having mistaken notions 8.Inability to hold on to what is achieved 9.Oscillating mind causing distraction and losing progress.

sections.insight: Challenges are natural on any path.  These are the nine obstacles physical, mental / intellectual and spiritual impediments in the path of yoga.
sections.practice: Observe the obstacle you are facing, intently.
sections.meditation: 20 min meditate on the challenge/s you have encountered in your practice

sections.wisdomFrom: You have a right to perform your prescribed duties, but you are not entitled to the fruits of your actions
sections.gurudevInsight: We considered the nine possible obstacles on the path of Yoga. Every possible obstacle has been counted, included in these 9 categories. Just few words, very few words, very concisely he has said all that is to be said, that was needed to be said. Along with these nine obstacles, the 5 indications or signs of disturbed mind is mentioned.

sutra.meaning:
Sorrow, despair, unsteadiness of the body and irregular breathing further distract the chitta.

Adherence to single minded effort prevents these impediments.

sections.insight:
During meditation the body and mind feel restless.


Single minded focus reduces distraction.
sections.reflectionPrompt: How does my body and mind feel?
sections.practice: Whenever there is free time ponder about the obstacles to your practice. Why are they there?
sections.meditation:
5 min breathing, observe physical and mental state.
Meditate for 20 min
sections.journalPrompt: What did I feel physically? How was my meditation today?
sections.shlokaFrom:

न चाति स्वप्नशीलस्य जाग्रतो नैव चार्जुन || 6.16||
sections.wisdomFrom: O Arjuna, there is no possibility of becoming a yogi if one eats too much or eats too little, sleeps too much or does not sleep enough.
sections.gurudevInsight: Along with these nine obstacles, the 5 indications or signs of disturbed mind is mentioned i.e. 1) Dukha: Sadness/Sorrow 2) daurmanasya: Bitterness 3) agmajayatva: Restlessness in the body or lack of coordination in the body and 4) shwasprashwas: Irregular breathing. If you have observed your breath, when you are happy or excited, the incoming breath is longer, you are more aware of the incoming breath in a state of excitement & when you are unhappy, the outgoing breath is more prominent, you observe the outgoing breath, total imbalance of the breath happens.

sutra.meaning:
Discipline in practice, self-study, study of the scriptures and surrender to God are the acts of yoga.

Yoga reduces suffering and prepares for meditation.

sections.gurudevInsight: This aspect sharpens the intellect, softens the mind, the heart. “Tapaswadhyayaishwarapranidhana kriyayoga” Sadhanapath means on practices, on the path. Action is part & parcel of this creation. There is activity in every thing in creation. Right from an atom, to the Sun, Moon & stars, there is activity. There is nothing that is stable in this creation or immobile, everything is very active.
